messages.content: You are an illustrator who writes zpup scenes by hand. The zpup reference is below. Draw the requested subject as one zpup scene in JSON, 400 by 400 pixels. Make it look three-dimensional: give the parts volume and depth, and make it clear which parts are in front of others. Use only what zpup itself provides. Write plain JSON, not TypeScript or JavaScript. Reply with the JSON scene only: no explanation and no Markdown code fence. # zpup > zpup renders round, flat pseudo-3D illustrations (in the style of Zdog) from a plain JSON scene tree to an SVG string. ESM-only TypeScript, no runtime dependencies, no DOM needed. ## Entry points The npm package is `@zpup/core`. ```ts import { renderSvg, renderSpinSvg, checkScene, compileScene, ZpupValidationError } from '@zpup/core'; import { group, path, dot, ellipse, rect, polygon, box, cylinder, cone, hemisphere } from '@zpup/core'; // optional typed helpers renderSvg(scene, { precision: 2 }) // -> "\n" (pure, deterministic) checkScene(scene) // -> ValidationIssue[] (empty when valid), never throws checkSceneWarnings(scene) // -> ValidationIssue[]: valid but suspicious (radians, off-screen, draws nothing) compileScene(scene) // -> Frame: projected, depth-sorted 2D draw items renderSpinSvg(scene, options?) // -> "` and GitHub READMEs. Without SMIL support the first frame shows, identical to `renderSvg(scene)`. ```ts { axis?: 'x' | 'y' | 'z', // default 'y': adds the turning angle to scene.rotate.y (a turntable) duration?: number, // seconds per turn, >= 0.1, default 8 keyframes?: number, // integer 4..720, default 36; more = smoother and larger direction?: 'positive' | 'negative', // default 'positive': the angle grows precision?: number, // integer 0..10, default 1 } ``` Unknown or invalid options throw `ZpupValidationError` with paths such as `options.duration`. Only a constant turn about one axis is possible; nothing else in the scene moves. Keep scenes small (tens of shapes): file size grows with the number of pieces and of overlapping pairs. Use opaque colors; translucent outlines show seams. ## Examples Sphere with a ring: ```json { "width": 120, "height": 120, "rotate": { "x": -20, "y": 30 }, "children": [ { "type": "path", "path": [{}], "stroke": 40, "color": "#e62" }, { "type": "ellipse", "diameter": 70, "stroke": 5, "color": "#636", "rotate": { "x": 90 } } ] } ``` Face with grouped features: ```ts import { dot, group, path, renderSvg } from '@zpup/core'; const svg = renderSvg({ width: 160, height: 160, rotate: { y: -25 }, children: [ group({ id: 'head', children: [ dot({ stroke: 90, color: '#f4c95d' }), dot({ translate: { x: -16, y: -8, z: 40 }, stroke: 10, color: '#222' }), dot({ translate: { x: 16, y: -8, z: 40 }, stroke: 10, color: '#222' }), path({ id: 'smile', translate: { y: 12, z: 42 }, path: [{ x: -14 }, { bezier: [{ x: -7, y: 10 }, { x: 7, y: 10 }, { x: 14 }] }], stroke: 5, color: '#222', }), ], }), ], }); ``` A longer example lives in `examples/pup.ts`. ## Common mistakes - Radians (`1.57`, `Math.PI / 4`) -> angles are degrees (`90`, `45`). - Origin at the top-left as in SVG -> (0, 0) is the center; x and y run from -width/2 to width/2. Negative `y` is up. - `fill: "#fff"` -> `fill` is true or false; the color goes in `color`: `"color": "#fff", "fill": true`. - `stroke: "#000"` or `"12px"` -> `stroke` is a width in scene units (`2`); its color is `color`. - `type: "circle"` -> `"ellipse"` with `diameter`. `"line"` -> `"path"` with two points. `"sphere"` -> a dot (`path` `[{}]` with a thick stroke). `"cube"` -> `"box"`. - `radius` on an ellipse or round solid -> `diameter`. `height` on a cylinder or cone -> `length`. - `color` on a `group` -> set it on the shapes inside. ## Not available yet Canvas rendering, animation other than `renderSpinSvg`'s constant turn, perspective, React or other framework bindings.
